title: The Incremental Automation Framework
subtitle: A practical framework for automating complex, customized business processes in batches - not all at once. Built for ops teams with messy, real-world workflows.

intro.paragraph: You made the right call. This framework is exactly how I approach complex, customized processes with clients - the kind where "Kentucky does it differently than Texas" and suddenly your automation dream turns into a nightmare. Read through once, figure out which phase you're in, then pick ONE process to start with. That's it.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.html:
Here's what I see constantly: someone decides they want to automate their operations. They get excited. They try to automate everything at once. Three months later, they've spent a ton of money, nothing works reliably, and they're back to doing things manually while paying for software they don't use.

The problem isn't automation. The problem is approach.

Complex business processes - especially the ones that are "a little bit custom" depending on the situation - can't be automated in one shot. I mean, I just can't do the whole thing in a few hours. It's a really long thing to do. But if you wanna go slowly, we can slowly automate things and go with that.

That's not me being lazy. That's me being realistic about what actually works.

When you have processes that vary by region, by client tier, by compliance requirements, by whatever - you need a different strategy. You need to automate in batches. You need to build incrementally. You need to validate as you go.

This guide gives you that framework.

sections.title: The Core Problem With "Automate Everything"
sections.html:
Let me paint a picture. You have a process - let's say it's something like generating compliance documents. Sounds simple enough. But then:

  • Kentucky has different requirements than Texas
  • Your enterprise clients need different formatting than your SMB clients
  • Some projects need 15 fields populated, others need 40
  • There are edge cases that only your most experienced team members know about
highly customized process

When you try to automate a highly customized process all at once, you end up with one of two outcomes:

1. The automation is so rigid it breaks constantly - because it can't handle the variations
2. The automation is so complex nobody can maintain it - because you tried to account for every edge case upfront

Neither is good. Both waste money and time.

sections.title: The Batch Approach: How Incremental Automation Actually Works
sections.html:
Instead of trying to automate the whole process, you automate in batches. Each batch is a contained piece that you can build, test, and validate before moving on.

Phase 1: Map the Variations

Before you automate anything, you need to understand what actually varies. I'm talking about documenting:

  • Geographic variations - what's different by state, region, country
  • Client-type variations - what's different by tier, industry, size
  • Process-type variations - what's different by project type, service type, product type
  • Compliance variations - what's different by regulatory requirement
    • Process Step: Document header | Standard Version: Company logo + date | Variation 1: State-specific disclaimer (KY) | Variation 2: State-specific disclaimer (TX) | Variation 3: Enterprise client custom header
    • Process Step: Required fields | Standard Version: 15 core fields | Variation 1: +5 compliance fields | Variation 2: +3 compliance fields | Variation 3: +10 client-specific fields
